chapter_seo_title: Li Huowang Interrogates Bai Sai — A Masked Man, a Heated Stone, and a Hanged Wuchang
chapter_meta_description: Li Huowang grills Bai Sai about the mysterious attack on Niuxin Village, but Hongzhong’s whispered warning hangs over every answer. At night, a hanged white Wuchang demands to know: why did he ruin its business?
og_title: A Heated Stone, a Masked Man, and a Hanging Wuchang
og_description: Li Huowang doesn’t trust Bai Sai’s story, but he can’t prove it wrong. Then the dream pulls him into a mist where a hanged white Wuchang has a question for him.
twitter_title: The White Wuchang wants an answer.
twitter_description: Li Huowang thinks he’s in control. The dream proves otherwise. A hanged white Wuchang appears and asks: “Why did you ruin my business?”

lore_anchors.definition: The clan head of the Bai family from Niuxin Village. He presents himself as grateful and cooperative, but his evasive answers draw immediate suspicion from Li Huowang.
One of the two emissaries of the Chinese underworld, traditionally the benevolent one who guides good souls. In the Dao-Twisted World, the image is weaponized as a terror tool.
A face-covering woven from old Chinese coins, used by jianghu outlaws to conceal identity. In the Dao-Twisted World, it also provides concealment from supernatural perception.
The home village of Bai Lingmiao’s family, led by clan head Bai Sai.
A traditional Chinese punishment device: a heavy wooden frame locked around the prisoner’s neck, hindering movement and serving as public humiliation.
